t: I will give thanks to/ you
I will sing praises to/ you

x.ASV: A Psalm of David. I will give thee thanks with my whole heart: Before the gods will I sing praises unto thee.
x.Darby: [A Psalm] of David. I will give thee thanks with my whole heart; before thegods will I sing psalms of thee.
x.KJV: A Psalm of David. I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
x.YLT: By David. I confess Thee, with all my heart, Before the gods I do praise Thee.

nt: Here the **heart** represents the seat of a person’s emotions and will. David is saying that he will thank Yahweh with complete devotion. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with all of my being]

Here, **the gods** could refer to: (1) idols of other nations that the psalmist sees either within Israel or while traveling. Alternate translation: [idols of foreign gods] or (2) God’s heavenly council of angelic beings. Alternate translation: [the heavenly assembly]

t: so/ I may give thanks to

x.ASV: I will worship toward thy holy temple, And give thanks unto thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: For thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.
x.Darby: I will bow down toward the temple of thy holiness, and celebrate thy name for thy loving-kindness and for thy truth; for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.
x.KJV: I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.
x.YLT: I bow myself toward Thy holy temple, And I confess Thy name, For Thy kindness, and for Thy truth, For Thou hast made great Thy saying above all Thy name.

nt: David is using the possessive form to describe a **temple** that is characterized by God’s **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your holy temple]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you, the Holy One] or [all that is holy about you]

David is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is and to refer to his reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who you are]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **trustworthiness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [the way you are faithful to your covenant and for being trustworthy]

The terms **covenant faithfulness** and **trustworthiness** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [your complete reliability]

The phrase **for you have exalted above all of your name your word** is a translation of the written Hebrew text. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed some alternative readings, and you may want to follow one of those. The UST follows the first alternative. Alternate translation: [for you have exalted above all else your name and your word] or [for you have exalted above all names your word]
David is using the term **word** to represent what Yahweh has spoken. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all that you have spoken]

x.ASV: In the day that I called thou answeredst me, Thou didst encourage me with strength in my soul.
x.Darby: In the day when I called thou answeredst me; thou didst encourage me with strength in my soul.
x.KJV: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.
x.YLT: In the day I called, when Thou dost answer me, Thou dost strengthen me in my soul with strength.

nt: David is using the word **soul** to refer to his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **power**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be mighty]

t: they will give thanks to/ you

x.ASV: All the kings of the earth shall give thee thanks, O Jehovah, For they have heard the words of thy mouth.
x.Darby: All the kings of the earth shall celebrate thee, Jehovah, when they have heard the words of thy mouth;
x.KJV: All the kings of the earth shall praise thee, O Lord, when they hear the words of thy mouth.
x.YLT: O Jehovah, all kings of earth confess Thee, When they have heard the sayings of Thy mouth.

nt: David is saying **all the kings of the earth** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [kings everywhere]

David is using **the words from your mouth** to represent everything that Yahweh has communicated. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the things you have declared]

x.ASV: Yea, they shall sing of the ways of Jehovah; For great is the glory of Jehovah.
x.Darby: And they shall sing in the ways of Jehovah, for great is the glory of Jehovah.
x.KJV: Yea, they shall sing in the ways of the Lord: for great is the glory of the Lord.
x.YLT: And they sing in the ways of Jehovah, For great is the honour of Jehovah.

nt: David is speaking of what Yahweh does as if those actions were **ways** or paths that he walks along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of what Yahweh does]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is very glorious]

x.ASV: For though Jehovah is high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly; But the haughty he knoweth from afar.
x.Darby: For Jehovah is high; but he looketh upon the lowly, and the proud he knoweth afar off.
x.KJV: Though the Lord be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly: but the proud he knoweth afar off.
x.YLT: For high is Jehovah, and the lowly He seeth, And the haughty from afar He knoweth.

nt: David uses the word **Though** here to indicate a contrast between Yahweh’s supreme status and his attention to those who are humble. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Even though Yahweh is high, he still sees the lowly]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s supreme status as if it were a physical height, saying **Yahweh is high**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is supreme]

David is using the adjective **lowly** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [yet he sees lowly people]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s relationship to proud people as if it involved physical distance, saying he **knows** them **from far off**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the proud he keeps at a distance]

David is using the adjective **proud** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and those who are proud]

x.ASV: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me; Thou wilt stretch forth thy hand against the wrath of mine enemies, And thy right hand will save me.
x.Darby: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou wilt stretch forth thy hand against the anger of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
x.KJV: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
x.YLT: If I walk in the midst of distress Thou quickenest me, Against the anger of mine enemies Thou sendest forth Thy hand, And Thy right hand doth save me.

nt: David uses the word **Though** here to indicate a contrast between the danger he faces and the protection Yahweh provides. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Despite that I walk in the middle of trouble, you will still keep me alive]

Here David is speaking of experiencing danger as if it were a place through which he walks, saying he will **walk in the middle of trouble**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I experience great trouble]

Here, **hand** represents Yahweh’s power to act. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you will use your power]

Here, **nose** represents the anger of David’s enemies. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the anger of my enemies]

Here, **right hand** represents Yahweh’s power to deliver. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will powerfully save me]

x.ASV: Jehovah will perfect that which concerneth me: Thy lovingkindness, O Jehovah, endureth for ever; Forsake not the works of thine own hands.
x.Darby: Jehovah will perfect what concerneth me: thy loving-kindness, O Jehovah, [endureth] for ever; forsake not the works of thine own hands.
x.KJV: The Lord will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
x.YLT: Jehovah doth perfect for me, O Jehovah, Thy kindness is to the age, The works of Thy hands let not fall!

nt: By **Yahweh will accomplish for my benefit**, the psalmist means that whatever Yahweh does will be to fulfill his purpose for David. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will accomplish his purpose for my benefit]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the way you are faithful to your covenant]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please do not forsake the works of your hands]

Here, **the works of your hands** represents what Yahweh has made and accomplished. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what you have made]
